description: Alerts subsystem: alert channels (MS Teams via fetch, Nodemailer email with sendRaw), the cooldown tracker, the alert engine (event-driven + sampled rules with maintenance gating and allSettled dispatch isolation), and the daily digest scheduler. Depends on FEAT-001 (state hub, error tracker, metrics store, config, events) and FEAT-002 (metrics:tick, error:captured, process:transition semantics). Grounded in design.md 'Alert engine', 'Alert channels', 'Daily digest', 'Maintenance mode', the alert-rule schema, and the disjointness/MEDIUM-2/MEDIUM-3 rules.
steps: src/alerts/channels/types.ts: AlertChannel {name:'teams'|'email', enabled:boolean, send(payload:AlertPayload):Promise<void>}; AlertPayload {title, severity:'info'|'warning'|'critical', processName, ruleId, summary, facts:{k,v}[], timestamp, suppressedCount}; EmailChannel extends AlertChannel with sendRaw({subject,html,text}):Promise<void>.

src/alerts/channels/teams.ts: TeamsChannel.send builds a MessageCard JSON (themeColor by severity, activityTitle, facts section, process name + timestamp) and POSTs to TEAMS_WEBHOOK_URL via global fetch with Content-Type application/json and a 10s AbortController timeout; non-2xx/network/timeout rejects. enabled=false when TEAMS_WEBHOOK_URL absent (logged once). Keep the MessageCard builder a pure exported function. Add src/alerts/channels/teams.test.ts asserting the payload shape for each severity (pure builder; no network).

src/alerts/channels/email.ts: EmailChannel with a Nodemailer transport built once from SMTP config, verify()-ed at startup (failed verify disables channel + warn, does not abort boot); send(payload) sends HTML+text to MAIL_TO; sendRaw({subject,html,text}) sends a raw multi-recipient message (used by the digest). enabled=false when SMTP config absent. Keep the HTML/text builders pure where practical.

src/alerts/cooldown.ts: CooldownTracker — in-memory Map<string,{lastFired,suppressed}> keyed (ruleId,processName); allow(key, cooldownSec) returns whether a fire is permitted and rolls suppressed counts; injectable clock. Add src/alerts/cooldown.test.ts (fire/suppress/reset timing).

src/alerts/engine.ts: AlertEngine holding AlertRule[], the CooldownTracker, and enabled channels. Event-driven evaluation wired to MonitorEvents: errored on process:transition to==='errored'; unexpected-stop on transition to stopped/exit the token model classified unexpected; restart-threshold on error:captured level restart intentional===false via ErrorTracker.restartsInWindow(name,rule.withinMin*60) firing at rule.count; error-spike on error:captured level error via ErrorTracker.countInWindow(name,rule.withinSec) firing at rule.count. Sampled evaluation subscribed to metrics:tick (AFTER MonitorState subscribes) running cpu-threshold/mem-threshold via MonitorState.getMetrics -> MetricsStore.sustainedAbove(forSec). Switch over rule.match.condition.type narrows via the discriminated union. On match: build AlertPayload, cooldown gate with suppressedCount rollup ('+N more since last alert'), maintenance gate (when active: record in recent-alerts list + WS alert with delivered:false + log, dispatch to NO channel), else dispatch to targeted channels via Promise.allSettled (one failure logged warn, never throws/blocks the other). Expose a recent-alerts accessor, a reload(rules) that recomputes the tracker max window, and a test(channel) path for POST /api/alerts/test. Add src/alerts/engine.test.ts with a fake state hub, injected clock, and spy channels asserting cooldown, maintenance gating, allSettled isolation, and the restart-threshold/error-spike/sustained wiring.

src/alerts/digest.ts: a scheduler computing the next DIGEST_HOUR local-time occurrence via setTimeout (reschedules daily); on fire build the digest (per-process status table, restart counts, top error signatures = signatures whose lastSeen is within 24h ranked by all-time count desc top N, labeled an approximation bounded by ERROR_BUFFER_SIZE, total alerts dispatched/suppressed) and send via EmailChannel.sendRaw; independent of maintenance mode; a send failure warns and does not stop the schedule. Only active when DIGEST_ENABLED and the email channel is configured. Add src/alerts/digest.test.ts (next-fire computation across hour boundaries + digest payload builder, injected clock).
acceptance_criteria: npm run build compiles with ZERO TypeScript errors.
npm test passes for cooldown, engine, teams payload builder, and digest tests.
The engine dispatches via Promise.allSettled so one channel throwing neither crashes the app nor blocks the other (asserted by test).
Maintenance mode records+logs the alert with delivered:false and dispatches to no channel while active (asserted by test).
Sampled rules evaluate on metrics:tick after MonitorState has pushed that tick's samples; restart-threshold consults restartsInWindow (crash-loop restarts only).
verification: Run: npm run build  — zero tsc strict errors.
Run: npm test  — alerts subsystem tests pass (cooldown, engine, teams, digest).
findings:
VERIFIED: npm run build => 0 tsc strict errors; npm test => 117 pass / 0 fail (87 FEAT-001+002 + 30 new FEAT-003 across src/alerts: cooldown 5, teams 4, engine 12, digest 9). PM2 daemon NOT running (pgrep confirms none). No real SMTP/Teams network: Teams builder is pure + tested with no fetch; engine/digest tests use spy channels; no AbortController/fetch exercised in tests.

TEST-SCRIPT FIX (package.json, the FEAT-001-predicted revisit): FEAT-001's unquoted `tsx --test src/**/*.test.ts` only matched one dir deep (sh ** acts as *), so the two-dirs-deep src/alerts/channels/teams.test.ts was silently skipped by `npm test` while `npx tsx --test 'src/alerts/**/*.test.ts'` (tsx expands ** itself) still found it. FEAT-003's AC requires `npm test` to run the teams builder test, so I changed the test script to be depth-agnostic: test="tsx --test $(find src -name '*.test.ts')" (npm runs scripts via sh; $(find ...) command substitution collects every *.test.ts at any depth). Verified: npm test now reports 117 tests incl. the 4 buildTeamsCard tests. A quoted recursive glob was rejected (confirmed: Node/tsx cannot expand 'src/**/*.test.ts' on this Node 20.19 => 'Could not find').

NEW FILES (all under src/alerts/): channels/types.ts, channels/teams.ts, channels/teams.test.ts, channels/email.ts, cooldown.ts, cooldown.test.ts, engine.ts, engine.test.ts, digest.ts, digest.test.ts. No existing files modified (FEAT-001/002 untouched).

channels/types.ts EXPORTS: type AlertSeverity ('info'|'warning'|'critical'); interface AlertPayload {title,severity,processName,ruleId,summary,facts:{k,v}[],timestamp,suppressedCount}; interface AlertChannel {name:'teams'|'email', enabled:boolean, send(payload):Promise<void>}; interface RawMessage {subject,html,text}; interface EmailChannel extends AlertChannel {name:'email', sendRaw(msg:RawMessage):Promise<void>}.

channels/teams.ts EXPORTS: buildTeamsCard(payload): TeamsMessageCard (PURE, exported — themeColor by severity info=2EB886/warning=E3B341/critical=D23F31, title+summary, one section with activityTitle=processName, activitySubtitle=ISO ts, facts [Process,Rule,Severity,Time,...payload.facts, +Suppressed when >0], text=summary); interface TeamsMessageCard; class TeamsChannel implements AlertChannel (opts {webhookUrl?,logger?,fetchFn?,timeoutMs?=10000}; enabled=false + warnOnce('teams-disabled') when webhookUrl absent; send() POSTs via injectable fetchFn with Content-Type application/json + 10s AbortController; non-2xx or network/timeout rejects).

channels/email.ts EXPORTS: buildAlertText/buildAlertHtml(payload) (PURE, exported, HTML-escaped); interface SmtpConfig {host,port,secure,user,pass,from,to(raw comma MAIL_TO)}; interface MailTransport {verify(),sendMail(...)}; interface EmailChannelOptions {smtp?,logger?,createTransport?}; class EmailChannel implements channels/types EmailChannel. enabled=false when smtp absent (warnOnce 'email-disabled'). verify() disables channel (sets enabled=false) + warn on failure, NEVER throws (boot continues). send() -> sendMail HTML+text subject '[severity] title'. sendRaw() -> raw subject/html/text. createTransport default wraps nodemailer.createTransport({host,port,secure,auth:{user,pass}}); FEAT-004 passes smtp built from SMTP_* + MAIL_FROM/MAIL_TO and MUST await channel.verify() at boot.

cooldown.ts EXPORTS: interface CooldownDecision {allowed,suppressedCount}; class CooldownTracker (opts {now?}); allow(ruleId,processName,cooldownSec): first call fires (suppressed 0); within window -> allowed:false and increments running suppressed; after >=cooldownSec elapsed since lastFired -> allowed:true carrying the prior suppressed rollup then resets it. Key is (ruleId,processName). reset() clears all. Clock injectable.

engine.ts EXPORTS: const not exported; interface AlertStateHub {getMaintenance():{active}, getProcess(name), processNames():string[], sustainedAbove(name,'cpu'|'mem',threshold,durationSec):boolean}; interface AlertErrorWindows {countInWindow(name,sinceSec), restartsInWindow(name,sinceSec), setMaxWindow(sec)}; interface RecentAlert {payload,delivered}; interface AlertEngineOptions {rules,state,events,errors,channels,defaultCooldownSec,logger?,cooldown?,now?,recentLimit?=200}; class AlertEngine; isErroredStatus(status) helper.
  WIRING (binding for FEAT-004 bootstrap): engine subscribes in ctor to process:transition, error:captured, metrics:tick. metrics:tick MUST be subscribed AFTER MonitorState (MonitorState constructed before AlertEngine) so samples are pushed first. Condition->trigger map: errored => process:transition to==='errored'; unexpected-stop => error:captured level 'crash' && message==='process exited unexpectedly' (the Pm2Client unexpected-exit marker; this keeps it DISJOINT from errored and from a process:exception crash whose message differs); restart-threshold => error:captured level 'restart' && intentional===false, fires when errors.restartsInWindow(name, withinMin*60) >= count; error-spike => error:captured level 'error', fires when errors.countInWindow(name, withinSec) >= count; cpu-threshold/mem-threshold => evaluated once per metrics:tick over processes PRESENT in that tick via state.sustainedAbove(name,'cpu'|'mem',threshold,forSec). processes:['*'] matches all present (sampled) / the event's process (event-driven); otherwise the rule's explicit name list. On match: buildPayload -> cooldown.allow gate (sets payload.suppressedCount from the rollup) -> maintenance gate: if active, record(delivered:false) + emit 'alert' {delivered:false} + log, NO channel dispatch; else record(delivered:true) + emit 'alert' {delivered:true} + dispatch via Promise.allSettled over the rule's targeted+enabled channels (a rejected settle logs warn, never throws/blocks the other). A rule toggling a channel that is !enabled is skipped for that channel (warnOnce). reload(rules) swaps rules + recomputes errors.setMaxWindow(max(error-spike withinSec, restart-threshold withinMin*60, 60s floor)) (also called in ctor). recentAlerts(limit?) returns the ring (cap recentLimit). test('teams'|'email') sends a probe AlertPayload to that channel (rejects if the channel is not in the configured list) — for POST /api/alerts/test.
  NOTE for FEAT-004: AlertEngine needs an AlertStateHub adapter — MonitorState exposes getMaintenance/getProcess but NOT processNames or sustainedAbove. Bootstrap must wrap: processNames()=state.snapshot().processes.map(p=>p.name) (or similar) and sustainedAbove delegating to the hub-owned MetricsStore.sustainedAbove (the hub boundary — do NOT reach MetricsStore from the engine directly; pass a thin adapter). AlertErrorWindows is satisfied directly by ErrorTracker (countInWindow/restartsInWindow/setMaxWindow all exist on it).

digest.ts EXPORTS: interface DigestDataSource {processes():ProcessSnapshot[], trackedErrors(name):TrackedError[]}; interface AlertCounters {dispatched():number, suppressed():number}; interface DigestSchedulerOptions {email:EmailChannel,source,counters,digestHour,enabled,errorBufferSize,topN?=10,logger?,now?,setTimer?,clearTimer?}; class DigestScheduler. start() no-ops unless enabled && email.enabled; schedule() uses a self-rescheduling setTimeout to the next local DIGEST_HOUR (nextFireAt: today's hour if strictly future, else tomorrow; strictly-future so exactly-at-hour rolls to tomorrow). fire() builds + email.sendRaw; a send failure warns, never throws, schedule continues. build() -> RawMessage {subject,text,html}: per-process status/restarts/instances table (sorted by name), Alerts dispatched/suppressed from counters, top-N error signatures = those with lastSeen within last 24h ranked by all-time count desc, labeled an approximation bounded by ERROR_BUFFER_SIZE. Independent of maintenance mode. Clock + timers injectable.
  NOTE for FEAT-004: DigestDataSource.processes() = MonitorState.snapshot().processes; trackedErrors(name) = ErrorTracker.list(name). AlertCounters must be fed by period dispatched/suppressed totals — the AlertEngine does NOT currently expose these counters, so FEAT-004 either tallies 'alert' events (delivered true=dispatched / false during maintenance; cooldown-suppressed matches are not emitted so a dedicated counter on the engine would be more accurate) or adds a small counter. Pass errorBufferSize=config.ERROR_BUFFER_SIZE, digestHour=config.DIGEST_HOUR, enabled=config.DIGEST_ENABLED.

TEST INFRA: node:test + node:assert via tsx. Engine tests use a FakeStateHub + FakeErrorWindows + SpyChannel (one can be constructed to throw) + injected clock + a setTimeout(0) flush to settle the allSettled dispatch. Digest tests build local-time timestamps with new Date(y,m,d,h,...) so nextFireAt assertions are timezone-independent, and no-op setTimer/clearTimer so no real timer runs. Teams builder tested purely (no fetch). The channels tests live two dirs deep (src/alerts/channels/teams.test.ts) and are collected by the new find-based npm test script (see TEST-SCRIPT FIX above).
